Toolchain: gofmt -l clean, go vet clean, golangci-lint 2.13.1 reports 0 issues over internal/reviewlog, internal/runchain, internal/status and internal/fsm/sandbox. No TODO/FIXME markers, no eval or other unsafe execution, and every chunk in this shard is part 1/1 (no truncated context).

findings.note: sandbox.Materialize fails the entire batch when two input paths resolve to the same destination, and its own 0o444 mode is what makes it fail. os.WriteFile on a path already written in this call returns EACCES, so Materialize returns (nil, "open .../head/internal/x.go: permission denied"). Verified empirically: Materialize(root, "B", "H", []string{"internal/x.go", "./internal/x.go"}, show) and the exact-duplicate case both fail this way. This is reachable in production. escalation.go:63-77 dedups by RAW string, but AllReferencedPaths yields "./internal/x.go" for ordinary judge prose ("compare with ./internal/x.go") while changedPaths yields "internal/x.go" - two distinct keys, one destination after filepath.Clean. The consequence is not local: escalationFor returns the error, adjudicateExec.resolve caches it under sync.Once (kind.go:563), and secondOpinion then marks EVERY cross-file rejection in the run VerdictCheckedButUnverified. Escalation is on by default precisely because "a false reject is the dangerous direction - it drops a real finding and nothing says so" (escalation.go:17); a reviewer writing a leading-./ path silently turns that protection off for the whole run. Two contributing defects: (a) Materialize does not dedupe the cleaned destination, and is therefore also not idempotent - a second call on the same root fails identically; (b) the WriteFile and MkdirAll errors are returned bare at sandbox.go:69 and 71, with no "sandbox:" prefix and no path, unlike the show error at line 66 which does wrap and name the path - so the operator sees only a permission-denied on a temp directory metareview created itself. No test covers a duplicate path, a ./-prefixed path, or a re-used root.

have[p] dedups on the raw string, never on filepath.Clean(p)

findings.note: Materialize's containment refusal is batch-fatal on input that is not a diff, and a comment elsewhere states the opposite cost. sandbox.go:44-45 justifies the refusal with "the path list ultimately derives from a diff and a diff is data" - but escalation.go:35 appends judge-authored paths from AllReferencedPaths, and diffselect.go:299-301 tells the reader that anything spurious "is filtered by existence when the evidence tree is built, and at worst costs one escalation." Neither half holds for an escaping path: it is refused before any existence check, and by the resolve/sync.Once caching it costs every escalation in the run, not one. Verified: AllReferencedPaths returns "../shared/util.go" for the prose "see ../shared/util.go for the other copy" - a path a reviewer writes without thinking - and Materialize refuses it. This is the defect class the comment is supposed to prevent: a comment that talks the reader out of a check the code needs. Skipping a non-contained path (recorded, so the omission is auditable) contains the blast radius to that one file; refusing the batch does not. The four inputs in TestMaterializeRefusesEscapingPaths all assert the refusal is correct, and none asserts anything about what the refusal costs.

evidence.note: "the path list ultimately derives from a diff" - it also derives from judge output

"at worst costs one escalation" - it costs all of them for the run

findings.note: TreeHash does not have to be an address for the suite to pass. Mutation: replace the per-file hash line with the digest alone, dropping side.dir and clean - `go test ./...` stays fully green. Under that mutation the hash collides in two ways I confirmed with a probe: a file present only at head collides with the same file present only at base (an addition and a deletion get one address), and a.go collides with z.go at identical content (a rename is invisible). The shipped code is correct - the same probe against the unmutated code reports no collision - but nothing pins it. That matters more here than for an ordinary guard: the package doc calls this the thing that "makes the audit honest ... content-addressing the tree restores it" (sandbox.go:9-11) and the field comment says "content address of everything written, so a verdict is replayable" (sandbox.go:38). Three tests exercise TreeHash and each pins a different dimension (content, revision, input order); the two that separate an address from a plain content digest - which path, and which side - are the two nobody pins. Add a case where head-only and base-only content hash differently, and one where two paths carrying identical bytes hash differently.

"content address of everything written, so a verdict is replayable" - the claim the mutation falsifies

findings.note: The only production change in this shard's fold.go chunk is untested. Reverting internal/fsm/run/fold.go:561 to the pre-0.9.0 shortOK(d.Kind, d.Model, d.Effort, d.InputHash, d.Error) - i.e. removing d.Evidence, d.TreeHash, d.BaseSHA and d.HeadSHA from withinCaps entirely - leaves `go test ./...` green, and no behavioural shell test can distinguish it either, since the values in play (a 64-hex tree hash, 40-hex SHAs, the literal EvidenceSandbox) are all far under MaxShort = 1024. withinCaps is the audit store's admission check: whether an oversized field is rejected or silently accepted into an append-only log is exactly the kind of property the repository is otherwise careful to pin. A table case in internal/fsm/run feeding an LLMCallData with an over-MaxShort TreeHash and asserting withinCaps is false would kill the mutation.

findings.note: The jsonl migration left a doc comment describing a constant that no longer exists, and the pair of copies diverged. In internal/reviewlog/reviewlog.go the const declaration was deleted but its four-line doc comment was kept and reworded, so lines 17-20 are now a free-floating comment sitting immediately above `type Summary` and documenting an identifier absent from the package - `grep -n maxJSONLLineBytes internal/reviewlog/` matches the comment and nothing else. internal/runchain/runchain.go got the identical rewording but kept the const (line 17), so the same edit was applied to both copies and the deletion to only one. Both surviving comments also still assert "callers size the buffer two bytes larger," which neither package now does - that moved into jsonl.NewScanner - so a maintainer reading either file is told this package manages a buffer it no longer touches. gofmt, go vet and golangci-lint are all clean on this, so nothing mechanical will catch it. Separately and cosmetically, both files place the new internal/jsonl import inside the stdlib block (reviewlog.go:6, runchain.go:6) while keeping a separate module group below; gofmt tolerates it, goimports would not.

findings.note: TestReportIsMachineReadableAndNamesWhatMustBeCleared cannot fail. Report's must_clear and blocked tags carry no omitempty (status.go:41-42), so both string literals appear in every marshalled Report regardless of content. Proven by mutation: deleting the NEEDS_REVISION fixture on line 26 entirely (leaving `root := t.TempDir()` and an empty repository) leaves the test passing. The name promises the report "names what must be cleared"; the body asserts only that two struct tags exist, and the fixture it sets up is decorative. The related gap is that the Blocker payload is almost entirely unpinned: blanking RunID, Verdict, Kind, Path, BlockingCount, AttemptNumber and MaxAttempts at status.go:72-73 and keeping only Target leaves `go test ./...` green, so every field the report exists to hand an operator can be dropped without a red test. Only Target survives, via the "task-c" substring check in TestEmitReportsExitOneWhenSomethingMustBeCleared. Making this test assert the fixture's target and run id appear in the marshalled must_clear entry would close both.

findings.note: The migration to the shared scanner is partial, and internal/jsonl's package doc overstates it as complete: "centralises the line cap shared by every reader of the repository's .jsonl files." Five readers were migrated on this branch (state, findings, fsm/record, runchain, reviewlog); four .jsonl readers still use bufio's 64 KiB default and would fail the whole file on one long line - internal/tasksource/tasksource.go:63 reading .beads/issues.jsonl, internal/knowledge/knowledge.go:73 reading metareview's own *.jsonl knowledge files, internal/epicsource/epicsource.go:86, and internal/sessionhistory/sessionhistory.go:226. Flagged low rather than blocking because none of those four files is in this diff (the branch did not regress them) and internal/jsonl/jsonl.go belongs to another shard - the claim itself should be narrowed or the remaining readers migrated, and the cross-shard reviewer is better placed to decide which. Raised here because reviewlog.go and runchain.go are two of the migrated copies in this shard, and "did every copy get the fix" is the question that migration invites.
